headline_marked: [[Vercel Sandbox runs AI code safely]] in isolated, ephemeral microVMs
headline: Vercel Sandbox runs AI code safely in isolated, ephemeral microVMs
summary: Vercel Sandbox isolates untrusted, AI-generated code in ephemeral Firecracker microVMs, preventing access to your application's secrets and environment variables.
details: Vercel Sandbox executes untrusted code, including AI-generated snippets, within isolated, ephemeral microVMs. This prevents model-written code from accessing your application's process, filesystem, or environment variables.

Running untrusted code via child_process.exec or eval in a Vercel Function's shared process exposes secrets like API keys and database URLs. A malicious snippet could exfiltrate data or starve CPU resources.

The Sandbox provisions a Firecracker microVM for each execution, the same virtualization technology AWS Lambda uses for tenant isolation. This offers a stronger security boundary than containers, making kernel-level escapes significantly harder.
Creating a sandbox is a single API call, allowing configuration of the base image, a hard timeout, and CPU resources. It's recommended to set the shortest possible timeout for each specific use case.

Always write generated code to a file inside the sandbox and run it as a subprocess; never pass model output directly through eval or the Function constructor. The runCommand() method returns stdout, stderr, and an exit code from the isolated process.

Sandboxes are ephemeral by design, with each create() call provisioning a fresh microVM and a clean filesystem. Any state needing to persist across runs must be stored externally, such as in a database or blob store.

Vercel Sandbox is not intended for trusted, self-authored code due to added latency, nor for full CI/build pipelines. It's specifically for scenarios where untrusted, model-generated, or user-submitted code genuinely needs to be executed.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide]], integrating team into ChatGPT development
headline: OpenAI acquires presentation startup NextSlide, integrating team into ChatGPT development
summary: NextSlide's AI tool transforms prompts, notes, and documents into polished presentations. Its team will now apply this mission to building AI products within ChatGPT.
details: OpenAI has acquired NextSlide, a startup specializing in AI-powered presentation generation. The NextSlide team is now integrated into OpenAI, where they will be working on ChatGPT.

NextSlide's core product was designed to convert various inputs like prompts, notes, documents, or research into editable, polished presentations. This aimed to streamline the creation of visual communication.

Founder Ahmed Beshry stated the startup's goal was to make visual communication more accessible, helping people express ideas clearly. This mission will continue at OpenAI, focusing on building AI products for creation and communication.
While the acquisition was announced recently, it actually took place "earlier this year," according to Beshry. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed by either company.
Beshry has a history with successful AI ventures, having previously co-founded Caper AI. Caper AI, a smart cart and cashier-less checkout startup, was acquired by Instacart in 2021.
